From the CEO's press note as India Today NE quotes it: 19,94,357 electors, 9,69,298 men, 10,24,735 women and 324 third gender. The press note itself was not found on ceomanipur.nic.in on 12 November. The report does not say whether service electors are included.

5,77,46,618 electors, 2,82,03,992 men, 2,95,34,734 women and 7,892 third gender, as The South First reported the consolidated draft roll. Dinakaran gives the same figures. The CEO's figures as Khas Khabar quotes them: 5,26,67,416 electors, 2,75,24,780 men, 2,51,42,052 women and 584 transgender. The report does not say whether the count covers all 200 seats. No press note on the draft was found on election.rajasthan.gov.in.

1,90,16,768 electors, 94,84,635 men, 95,31,721 women and 412 third gender, as Lalluram reports the draft roll. The report does not name the CEO's press note. Service electors and the names added and deleted were not given. No press note on the draft was on ceochhattisgarh.nic.in on the evening of 12 November.

PTI, as carried by ThePrint on 14 November 2026, gives the draft roll released on 12 November as 5,47,99,628 general electors, 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 third gender, which add up exactly. Against the final roll of 21 February 2026, which PTI gives as 5,39,81,065 electors (2,79,04,975 men, 2,60,75,186 women and 904 third gender), the rise is 8,18,563, made up of 3,80,169 men, 4,38,361 women and 33 third gender, which PTI gives from the Election Commission's figures. Dainik Bhaskar reports the same total, the same rise for men and women and the same third gender figures, and gives the men and women on the draft only in crore (2.82 and 2.65). The 71,530 service electors (68,978 men and 2,552 women), for 5,48,71,158 in all, are Bhaskar's figures, which PTI does not give. The 8,18,563 is a net change, and the names added and deleted since February were not reported. Bhaskar also reports 72,036 polling stations after 127 were added and 21 removed, and that claims and objections close on 11 December, are to be decided by 28 December, and the final roll is due on 4 January 2027. PTI gives the same closing date for claims and the same date for the final roll.

Dainik Jagran reports from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer 7,55,89,365 electors on the draft roll, of whom 3,99,16,747 are men, 3,56,71,129 are women and 1,489 are third gender. The paper sets them beside 7,46,91,135 electors in October 2025, the roll of the Assembly election, which is a rise of 8,98,230. The base in this file is the final roll of the intensive revision of 30 September 2025, so the change of 13,97,008 from it also takes in the 4,98,778 by which the roll grew between that final roll and the roll of the Assembly election of 2025. Hindustan Times on 13 November gives the draft as 75.5 million and about 1.3 million more than the 74.2 million after the intensive revision. No press note on the draft was on ceoelection.bihar.gov.in on 13 November, where the latest press note listed is dated 23 October 2026. Service electors and the names added and deleted since the final roll were not given.

The figures are the total row of the Chief Electoral Officer's summary of the draft electorate. The total of 2,73,60,254 includes 2,45,883 overseas electors, who are 2,06,943 men, 38,931 women and 9 third gender. General electors alone are 2,71,14,371, of whom 1,31,14,324 are men, 1,39,99,787 are women and 260 are third gender. The total with overseas electors is recorded here because the final roll of 21 February 2026 in final.csv counts them too. The CEO's statement as PTI reported it on ThePrint on 12 November gives the same total, men, women, third gender and number of overseas electors. A figure of 2,66,78,256 in a post by The South First on 12 November is not in the CEO's summary and was not used. Service electors and the names added and deleted since the final roll were not given.

From the Chief Electoral Officer's announcement as Pratidin Time reports it: 2,51,76,910 electors on the draft roll, of whom 1,25,87,650 are men, 1,25,88,939 are women and 321 are third gender. The report also gives 63,237 service electors and six overseas electors, and does not say whether the service or overseas electors are in the total. Assam was not in the intensive revision. The roll before this draft is the final roll of Assam's special revision of 10 February 2026, 2,49,58,139 electors, which is the figure the Assam pages carry. The report gives 4,12,344 names added and 1,93,573 deleted since then, a net rise of 2,18,771, and the figures add up for every sex.

From the CEO's press note F.No 16/4/2025-ELC of 12 November 2026, read from the scanned page because its text layer is damaged. The note puts the draft roll as on 12.11.2026 at 57,701 electors, 29,273 men, 28,428 women and no third gender electors. It says 639 of them are aged 18 or 19. It gives no count of service electors and no count of names added or deleted since the final roll of 14 February 2026.

The figures are those the Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Dr Vijay Kumar Jogdande, gave to the press, as Dainik Jagran and Aaj Tak reported them on 13 November 2026. The two reports agree on every figure. The draft roll holds 72,78,035 general electors, 37,93,373 men, 34,84,447 women and 215 third gender electors. Both reports give 86,028 service electors in addition, 83,352 men and 2,676 women, and the men, women and third gender add to the total without them. Names of 1,25,216 electors were added in a special campaign from 4 to 31 October 2026. The reports say 6,130 applications in Form 7 to delete names were decided, and they do not say how many names were deleted. The final roll of 3 October 2026 held 71,58,949 electors, and 71,58,949 plus 1,25,216 less 6,130 equals the draft exactly, which would be so if every one of those applications ended in a deletion. A second Jagran report gives the change since the final roll as 63,411 men and 55,672 women, and the two rolls give 55,672 more men and 63,411 more women, so that report has the two figures the wrong way round. The CEO's own press note on the draft was not on ceo.uk.gov.in on 14 November 2026, where the latest press note listed is of 22 October.

PTI, as carried by ThePrint on 17 November 2026, gives the figures the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, gave at a press conference in Lucknow on the day the draft roll was published. The draft roll holds 13,58,68,905 electors, 7,38,58,510 men, 6,20,06,353 women and 4,042 third gender, which add up exactly. Against the final roll of 10 April 2026 the net rise is 18,84,113, made up of 10,96,828 more women and 7,87,449 more men, with 164 fewer third gender electors. The names added and deleted since April were not reported. PTI gives 11,83,352 electors aged 18 or 19 on the draft, against 17,63,360 in April, and 840 women for every 1,000 men, against 834. The New Indian Express of 17 November, with inputs from PTI, gives the same total and the same numbers of men, women and third gender. The CEO's own press note was not read, because ceouttarpradesh.nic.in could not be reached on 17 November 2026. Service electors were not given.

The Chief Electoral Officer's press note on the draft, sent with letter No.4-1-2026/ELEC/2852 of 11 November 2026 for release on 12 November, gives the schedule and no figures, and no press note with figures was on ceogoa.nic.in on 17 November 2026. The figures are the sum of the number of electors printed on the cover page of each of the 1,735 part rolls of the 40 constituencies that the Chief Electoral Officer's website lists for the draft, each giving 12 November 2026 as its date of updation. The part rolls are lists of electors and are not linked here. The parts of constituency 25, Vasco-da-Gama, are scanned images and were read by eye, and they hold 27,063 electors, 13,513 men, 13,547 women and 3 third gender. The parts add to 10,89,381 electors, 5,26,441 men, 5,62,932 women and 8 third gender. The New Indian Express of 17 November gives a rise of 31,815 electors, or 3.01 per cent, to 10.89 lakh, and the final roll of 21 February 2026 of 10,57,566 plus 31,815 is 10,89,381 exactly. The 299 service electors, 292 men and 7 women, are the sum of the cover pages of the 40 rolls of service electors, and they are not in the total. The names added and deleted since the final roll were not given.

The Chief Electoral Officer (i/c) gave the figures at a meeting with the recognised political parties on 17 November 2026, the day the draft was published, as the administration's daily reported on 18 November. The report gives a gender ratio of 980, an elector population ratio of 601, EPIC coverage of 99.32 per cent and 415 polling stations, up from 411. Nicobar Times reported the same figures. No service electors were given.

No official count of the draft has been found. The Chief Electoral Officer's release of 12 November on the draft gives the schedule and no figures, and ceopunjab.gov.in could not be reached on 21 November. Punjabi Jagran reported on 18 November that the draft stayed equal to the final roll of the special revision, 2.01 crore, and reported the Chief Electoral Officer, Anindita Mitra, as saying that the applications received had not been processed because the rationalisation of polling stations came first and the summary revision was announced three days after the final roll of 12 October. The New Indian Express reported on 18 November that Punjab's draft remained unchanged at the final tally of 2.01 crore and, citing unnamed sources, that the forms will be processed during the claims and objections period, which ends on 11 December. The figure here is therefore the final roll of 12 October, 2,01,00,727 electors, as the two reports describe the draft, and is to be replaced by the Chief Electoral Officer's own count when one is found.
